A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same BA-LoRA research work. All 25 pages of each version, including Appendices A–D, are readable, and the text, equations, tables and figures support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V3 reports original NLG and NLU benchmark results, regularization ablations, rank and hyperparameter analyses, and feature visualizations in Section 4 and Appendix C.

after.justification: V4 retains original benchmark and ablation results, revises several outcomes, and adds training-time and memory measurements in Appendix D.1.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.3 revises the specified NLG spectral regularizer to use randomized-SVD estimates and normalize over the approximated spectrum. V3 gave a full-spectrum formula and mentioned partial SVD in implementation details. PiSSA initialization and the three-regularizer framework remain intact.

E1.justification: Training datasets and evaluation coverage remain the same: MetaMathQA, CodeFeedback, WizardLM-Evol-Instruct, GSM8K, MATH, HumanEval, MBPP, MT-Bench, GLUE and GLUE-X. The revised t-SNE caption identifies MNLI, which was already specified in v3. Resource measurements reuse existing GLUE coverage.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is retained in Tables 1–4, the rank study, and v3 Table 10/v4 Table 9. Full fine-tuning already appeared in the earlier rank figure despite its narrower caption. The new cost comparison uses the existing LoRA and PiSSA comparators.

E3.justification: Section 4.2 substantially revises stated regularization weights: NLU changes from (0.0001, 0.0004, 0.0001) to (0.1, 0.04, 0.01), and NLG from (0.0001, 0.0003, 0.0001) to (0.0001, 0.3, 0.1). These changes do not establish which experiments were rerun. Appendix D.1 also introduces training-time and memory evaluation using DeBERTa-v3-base on full GLUE with an A40 GPU.

E4.justification: V3 Appendix C.4/Figure 5 tests sensitivity to three regularization weights over 1e-6 through 1e-2; this analysis is removed. V3 Table 5's task-level NLU ablation evidence is reduced to aggregate scores in v4 Figure 3. V4 adds computational-overhead analysis. The rank study remains, with relocation and revised plotted results.

E5.justification: V4 first supplies ± quantities throughout Tables 1–4 and Appendix Table 9, substantially expanding uncertainty reporting. Both versions already state three independent runs and three seeds for the BERT/GPT-2 experiments, so an increased run count is not established. V4 does not define the ± statistic or explain entries such as 9.21±17.

E6.justification: Numerous table values and rank-study curves are revised. Table 1 changes LLaMA-2-7B BA-LoRA GSM8K from 53.83 to 54.53; Table 2 changes Full FT SST-2 from 95.61 to 96.33, overtaking unchanged BA-LoRA at 96.25. Sensitivity results and task-level single-regularizer scores disappear. New LoRA/PiSSA/BA-LoRA cost results are 14.45/12.07/15.82 hours and 6.3/6.5/7.1 GB. Revised settings preclude treating the score replacements as controlled performance gains.

T1.justification: Equation 12 changes its mathematical definition from singular values normalized over the full spectrum to estimated singular values, with D defined over the approximation. This exceeds a notation change. The remaining formal framework is retained, and no new theorem or proof appears.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the central claims: three regularizers mitigate inherited noise and imbalance while improving NLG/NLU performance over LoRA variants. The introduction's broader comparator wording and references to extended experiments restate claims already present in v3.

C2.justification: Appendix D.1 replaces explicit limitations with explanations of computational overhead, randomized-SVD scalability and an argument that added costs are justified. Related multilingual, fairness and adaptive-weighting concerns remain in future work. Removing the sensitivity section also removes its explanation of degradation under stronger regularization. The new cost discussion additionally invokes mitigation of catastrophic forgetting.

D1.justification: V4 newly specifies k=5 for NLU and k=10 for NLG, revises the documented regularization weights, and provides randomized-SVD and resource-measurement details. Most implementation instructions, Appendix B settings, hardware information and code/model access statements remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V4 adds Pasand and Bashivan's RGP work as support for randomized SVD. The revised and duplicated AdaLoRA references correspond to the previously cited work rather than additional distinct research. Broader positioning against PEFT and LoRA variants remains stable.

P1.justification: The rank analysis moves from Appendix C.2 to Section 4.4, the NLG/NLU ablation narrative is condensed into Section 4.5, and Appendix D.1 is rewritten around computational cost. Most introductory, methodological and background prose remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: Experimental displays are substantially reorganized. V3 Figure 2's grouped bars and Table 5 are replaced by v4 Figure 3's three line-chart panels, retaining only NLU averages. The rank figure is redrawn and moved into the main text, the sensitivity figure disappears, result tables are compressed to accommodate ± entries, and appendix figures are redistributed.

improvement.justification: V4 adds useful resource measurements, k settings and uncertainty reporting. However, the ± statistic is undefined, entries such as 9.21±17 are unexplained, and Table 1's prose retains a 1.82-point GSM8K advantage although its updated values imply 2.16. Removing weight-sensitivity results and task-level NLU ablations weakens support for the revised settings. These material benefits and losses do not establish a reliable net direction in overall quality.
